There’s a death spiral that goes like this: 

1. you’re tired so you hit snooze on difficult conversations

2. your backlog from 1 is overwhelming

3. You start spacing out in each other’s presence (how was your day? fine). life is now a series of chores

4. The “spark” is gone

title: Marriage: pick your favorite future annoyance
summary:
visakanv kicked this whole mini-canon off with a brutally sticky line in 2018: marriage is basically choosing the one person who’ll “upset, disappoint, annoy and frustrate you more than anybody else.” The hook was that it sounds like an anti-romance dunk, but his actual claim is more pragmatic: proximity turns even a low-annoyance person into your highest-annoyance person (base rates + shared consequences), so you’d better build systems for the inevitable friction instead of treating conflict as a sign you picked wrong.

Arc-wise it goes: **trigger (viral one-liner)** → **peak (turning it into relationship engineering)** → **outcome (it becomes a reusable reference thread people literally schedule reminders to reread).** In the peak phase, Visa expands it into frameworks: relationships need an “economy” (gratitude/laughter/kindness) plus “waste elimination” (deal with pain/resentment), and he drops the canonical “death spiral” model: snoozing hard conversations → backlog → you go numb around each other → everything feels like chores → spark dies → you become “play-acting corporate shells” fighting about dishes. By Dec 2018 he sharpens the moral: “I wasn’t thinking” stops being cute and becomes a hollow excuse; long-term love is a commitment to becoming more considerate. patio11 adds the companion warning: pick someone who sees your flaws as acceptable tradeoffs because they’ll be the one carrying most of the burden of dealing with them.

By 2021–2024 it stops being discourse and turns into lore: visakanv’s wife, sharanvkaur, posts the fridge-journal relic (“this boy is one of the things i’m sure i want”) and how it defused a fight by making her laugh mid-yell; tnorthcutt posts receipts of a twice-yearly calendar event titled “read Visa thread on marriage”; and Visa keeps iterating the core heuristic into sharper tools (“navigate by lows; highs degrade,” “bring your worst selves to the altar,” “love is easy—what’s harder is not hating each other”). If you’re dating/married and tired of soulmate narratives, this strand’s residue is a whole shared vocabulary—**economy vs trash, death spiral, fight fair, optimize for lows**—that lets you talk about marriage like a maintainable system instead of a vibe you’re failing to feel.
